conventions.value: the default used by the deck and the simulator
conventions.range: [low, high] used by slide sliders and by the one-at-a-time sensitivity sweep; null = structural, excluded from the sweep
conventions.rationale: why this value; any ledger fact named here is a sanity check, not the source of the number

facts._note: Chagee facts quoted on slides. Not assumptions: each carries its ledger source and appears with that source in the speaker notes.

tea_latte_share_china.rationale: Secondary source; flagged as such wherever shown.

signal_strength_default.unit: share, 0 = no pre-launch signal, 1 = strong signal
signal_strength_default.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 4 rework). Slide 2 slider default. Band half-width u = uncertainty_no_signal - signal x (uncertainty_no_signal - uncertainty_strong_signal), a straight line between the two approved end points. At 0.5, u = 32.5%. This u feeds slides 3 and 5.

remove_hype_default.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 4 rework). Slide 2 starts with opening-week hype removed, so slides 3-5 receive the steady-demand band by default. The hype band stays visible on the chart for comparison.

open_hours_per_day.rationale: Generic mall/high-street trading day (10:00-22:00). Structural: sets the length of the simulated day.

open_days_per_year.rationale: Allows for a few closure days. Only converts cups/year to cups/day.

cups_per_store_per_year.rationale: About 555 cups/day after the opening period. No public per-store cup figure in the ledger; GMV per store cannot be turned into cups without an average ticket price, which the ledger does not have. Wide range on purpose.

hourly_demand_share.unit: share of daily cups per open hour (10:00 to 22:00), sums to 1
hourly_demand_share.rationale: Lunch peak and an evening plateau, typical of a tea shop. Peak hour = 11% of the day. Structural; the surge setting tests peaks above it.

uncertainty_definition.rationale: Uncertainty u = (high - low) / 2 / base, as a % of the forecast base. This is exactly the band width that slide 2 outputs, and it is the x-axis of the slide 4 crossover chart.

band_coverage.rationale: The low-high band is an 80% interval: true demand = base x (1 + u x z / 1.2816), z standard normal. So 1 in 10 stores lands above high and 1 in 10 below low. An 80% band is a common planning interval; a 95% band would make the same u mean less spread.

demand_floor_share_of_base.rationale: Demand draws are floored at zero (user change; was 0.20). A draw can be a store with no demand. At u = 0.60, P(z < -2.14) is about 1.6% of draws.

uncertainty_no_signal.rationale: Slide 2: band before any pre-launch app signal, i.e. a judgement-led forecast in a new market. Illustrative.

uncertainty_strong_signal.rationale: Slide 2: band with a strong pre-launch waitlist signal. It does not reach zero because tourist and non-app demand stay invisible (named blind spot).

opening_hype_multiplier.rationale: Slide 2 toggle 'remove opening-week hype'. Sanity check only: L-gabgrowth reports 1,000+ cups on the KL opening day, about 1.8x our 555/day base, but that is one day, one store, from a secondary source.

opening_hype_weeks.rationale: How long the hype lasts before demand settles. Illustrative.

uncertainty_sweep.rationale: x-axis of the crossover chart. Covers strong-signal to no-signal bands from slide 2.

surge_multiplier.rationale: Slide 4 toggle. Applied to the two busiest hours. Default = moderate. The counter is sized to the forecast curve without the surge, so a surge is the unplanned peak that piles up behind fixed capacity.

surge_hours.unit: busiest forecast hours that get the surge
surge_hours.rationale: This number was only in the surge_multiplier rationale; it now has its own field so the code reads it from here. With the default curve these are 12:00-14:00 (ties go to the earlier hour).

surge_default.rationale: Default toggle position and printed state.

human_seconds_per_cup.unit: seconds of one average worker per cup
human_seconds_per_cup.rationale: Totals 60 s, so one average worker makes about 1 cup/min. Range is a multiplier on all six. Stylised benchmark: Chagee already uses QR-scan dispensing (L-unsw), so 'all-human' is a reference case, not Chagee's current counter.

machine_seconds_per_cup.unit: seconds per cup per machine unit
machine_seconds_per_cup.rationale: Topping/finish is the hardest step to automate, so it is the slowest machine (4 cups/min per unit). Range is a multiplier on all six. The high end, 2.0, puts the slowest station at 30 s (2 cups/min per unit), as the user asked; was 1.3. No public per-station machine times; Gong cha's company-reported productivity figures are not per station, so they are not used.

mixed_machine_stations.rationale: Fixed-time steps go to machines; cup/ice, topping/finish and handover (more variable) stay with people, who share the work including one flexible worker.

machine_speed_variation_cv.rationale: Machines run at a fixed speed (brief.md section 2). Machine breakdowns are not modelled; this flatters automation, and the slide will say so.

human_speed_variation_cv.unit: coefficient of variation, minute to minute
human_speed_variation_cv.rationale: Random minute-to-minute variation in a worker's pace.

worker_speed_spread.rationale: Workers differ in speed (slowest 0.8x, fastest 1.2x by default). This is what the bucket brigade rebalances.

coordination_loss_human.rationale: Pooling assumes perfect rebalancing. Handovers, walking and bumping at a small counter lose some of that. The Week 5 engine at realistic walk-back speed gives an information-only calibration point (see validation).

coordination_loss_mixed.unit: multiplier on human-pool throughput in the mixed setup
coordination_loss_mixed.rationale: Same as all-human by default; kept separate because people also wait on machines in the mixed line.

new_staff_share.unit: share of roster in first months
new_staff_share.rationale: Staff turnover lever on slide 4. A new store, and churn, mean a share of staff are new.

new_staff_relative_speed.rationale: New staff are slower until trained. With defaults, average speed falls to 0.925x.

min_staff_on_shift.rationale: A counter never runs with fewer people than this. All-machine uses attendant hours instead.

all_machine_attendant_per_open_hour.rationale: Restocking, cleaning, exceptions, customer help. Approved: all-machine is not zero labour.

staffing_flexibility.unit: share of roster gap closed after demand is known
staffing_flexibility.rationale: After opening, rosters move toward real demand; this share of the gap is closed (hiring, part-timers, shift changes). Machines get 0.

labour_cost_per_hour.unit: SGD per hour worked, fully loaded (statutory costs)
labour_cost_per_hour.source: L-mom-pwm, L-mom-ows, L-cpf, L-sdl, L-mom-leave, L-mom-ph
labour_cost_per_hour.rationale: APPROVED 9 Oct 2026 (was 14.09). Monthly gross S$2,295 = PWM minimum for a food service counter attendant from 1 Jul 2026 (L-mom-pwm); it binds because the June 2025 market medians are lower (barista S$2,242, counter attendant S$2,279 gross, L-mom-ows; MOM gross wage excludes employer CPF). Plus employer CPF 17% (L-cpf) and SDL 0.25% (L-sdl) = S$2,690.89 a month / 190.67 paid hours (44 h x 52 / 12) = S$14.11 per paid hour; x 286/268 for 18 paid days not worked (7 days annual leave in year 1, L-mom-leave; 11 public holidays, L-mom-ph) on a 5.5-day week (our assumption) = S$15.06 per hour worked. Still a floor: excludes sick leave, bonuses, training, recruitment, uniforms, foreign-worker levies and any 2026 pay above the minimum. Range low = the earlier CPF-only floor (S$14.09); high = USD 20 converted.

machine_cost_per_unit_per_month.unit: SGD per station machine unit per month
machine_cost_per_unit_per_month.rationale: Amortised purchase plus maintenance, cleaning and consumables. One rate for every station. No Chagee or industry figure in the ledger. Converted from the approved USD 1,500 (range 500-3,000) at fx_sgd_per_usd.

lost_order_cost.rationale: Margin on the cup not sold plus some goodwill. Charged when an order balks because the wait would exceed the target.

capacity_safety_margin.rationale: Same sizing rule for all three setups: capacity for forecast peak x margin. Machines round up to whole units, staff to whole workers.

target_wait_minutes.rationale: A slider, not a claim. An order balks if the wait it would see on arrival exceeds this. The call with Lee Yen mentioned a sub-one-minute fulfilment target, but that is informal and may mean prep time, not total wait; not used or cited.

milk_litres_per_cup.rationale: Milk in a tea latte. Illustrative; not a Chagee recipe figure.

milk_waste_cost_per_litre.rationale: Purchase cost of expired fresh milk. Overseas milk sourcing is unknown (ledger: do not claim), so this is generic.

milk_shelf_life_days.rationale: Generic chilled fresh milk. Stock held beyond this is wasted.

stockout_cost_per_cup.unit: SGD per cup not served for lack of stock
stockout_cost_per_cup.rationale: Set equal to lost_order_cost by default: a missed cup is a missed cup.

opening_stock_days.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 2 rework, changed from 3): slider start = the base forecast over one milk shelf life (provision.milk_shelf_life_days), i.e. the naive 'order the forecast' choice, so the cost-minimising order the calculator marks sits visibly above it. The first order is assumed to cover one shelf life before regular replenishment; stock beyond that window is wasted. The 3 previously approved was the slider start only and was mis-described as 'one shelf life'.

overseas_stores_per_year.rationale: About 200 overseas stores planned for 2026 (L-jiemian). The slide shows it as 'about 200' and as a slider.

saving_per_cup.rationale: Default = mixed vs all-machine cost-per-cup gap at the slide 2 default uncertainty and the default surge. Not hand-set.

waste_avoided.rationale: Default = slide 3 waste-plus-stockout saving from a narrower band. Not hand-set.

business_case._note: Appendix A4 revenue and cost analysis only. Costs of building and running the four gates. Never feeds the cost model in sim/. No sales revenue: there is no price or demand-elasticity assumption, so the benefit side is the modelled avoided cost from the benefit slide.

horizon_years.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Length of the A4 table, matching the five-year horizon of the course examples of a revenue and cost analysis.

opening_year_share.unit: share of a year a store trades in its opening year
opening_year_share.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Mid-year convention: openings spread evenly through the year, so a new store earns half a year of counter saving in its opening year. Openings are held flat at benefit.overseas_stores_per_year every year: L-jiemian covers 2026 only, so we assume no growth.

specialist_day_rate.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Blended rate for data, software and analyst staff, in-house or outsourced. No ledger figure; illustrative. Same structure as the course examples (people x days x rate).

working_days_per_month.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Standard working month, used to turn person-months into person-days.

build_people.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Year 1 build team, one per gate: demand forecast (Predict), ordering calculator (Provision), counter comparison (Counter), review dashboard (Review).

build_months.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Build and pilot in one market before roll-out.

integration_one_time.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Connecting POS sales, app membership sign-ups and supplier order feeds, plus hardware and software set-up. Lump sum, illustrative.

maintenance_people.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Keep the tools running, refresh assumptions, support market teams.

platform_per_store_month.unit: SGD per store in operation per month
platform_per_store_month.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Cloud, licences and dashboards for each store using the gates.

review_days_per_opening.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026).Gate 4: build the updated scenario from observed inputs and compare it with the original plan.

monte_carlo_draws.rationale: Enough for a smooth curve at build time; stability is checked across seeds.

base_seed.rationale: Fixed so every build gives the same numbers.

minute_step.rationale: Queue updated once per simulated minute.

live_draws.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 4 rework). Playbook 'Your market' panel: Monte Carlo draws per live verdict in the browser; equal to validation.crossover_stability.seeds. More is steadier but slower.

triggers._note: Added for brief-v2 (approved). Ranges searched by sim breakEven(); not new-store forecasts.

volume_trigger_range_cups_per_day.rationale: Approved for the volume trigger only and labelled on slides 'trigger range, not a new-store forecast'. Lower end = cups_per_store_per_year low (100,000) / open_days_per_year. Cost charts keep the approved 278-833 cups/day (cups_per_store_per_year range).

illustration._note: Slide 5 mechanism illustration only (approved). Dimensionless Week 5 units: speed 1 = one full line per hour. Never feeds the cost model.

worker_speeds.rationale: Week 5 Option 1 defaults (week5/build_opim639_deck.py SIM.option1.speeds), reused read-only.

base_load_share.unit: arrival rate as share of the crew's nominal capacity (sum of speeds)
base_load_share.rationale: Approved: base arrivals at 60% of the crew's capacity, so a surge (surge_multiplier) pushes the line past capacity.

value.matched: station rates = 3 x worker speeds (each station does a third of the work; same total speed as the crew)
value.as_sized: station rates scaled so the line's rate / crew nominal rate = all-machine / mixed peak-hour capacity in sim/ (default surge)

machine_sizing.rationale: Approved toggle: 'matched to the crew' shows the mechanism; 'as sized in our cost model' links to slide 6. The as-sized ratio is read from sim/ peakUtilisation(), not typed.

value.matched: machine block rate = the people part's nominal rate (crew speed / hand share), a balanced mixed line
value.as_sized: machine block rate scaled by mixed machine capacity / mixed peak-hour capacity in sim/ (default surge)

mixed_sizing.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 4 rework). Added for the combined bucket-brigade slide (user request after step 4): the mixed lane shows the machine stations (stations.mixed_machine_stations) as one fixed-rate block feeding a people brigade that pools the hand steps. The hand share is derived from stations.human_seconds_per_cup, not typed. The as-sized ratio is read from sim/ plan() and peakUtilisation(), not typed. Illustration only; never feeds the cost model.

machine_buffer_capacity.rationale: APPROVED 9 Oct 2026, illustration only: a small buffer so an upstream machine blocks when the next one is busy.

run_hours.rationale: APPROVED 9 Oct 2026, illustration only: one run of the animation.

surge_window_hours.unit: start and end hour of the surge within a run
surge_window_hours.rationale: APPROVED 9 Oct 2026, illustration only: the surge lasts one hour mid-run so the queue can build and then drain.

validation._note: Fixed before anything is run (addition 4). Changing these after seeing results needs explicit sign-off.

breakeven.rationale: Approved (brief-v2 section 6, as amended). breakEven() scans grid_points evenly over a lever's range with fixed seeds, refines each sign change by bisection until the bracket is narrower than tol_x_share_of_range of the range. Pass if the two setups are within tol_cost at the returned value, OR the bracket is that narrow and the cheaper setup changes across it: a 'step' crossing (staff and machines come in whole units), labelled 'step' on slides. grid_points (13, as the uncertainty sweep) added in step 0.

value.engine: Brigade() read from the ENGINE string in week5/build_opim639_deck.py, not modified
value.pass_rule: pooled throughput (sum of speeds, coordination loss = 1) within +/-3% of Week 5 measured throughput for both speed sets
value.info_only: same comparison at walk = 6 (Week 5 Option 1 default); the gap is reported as a calibration point for coordination_loss, not pass/fail

week5_comparison.rationale: walk = 40 is Week 5's 'near-instant walk back, as the lecture assumes', which is what the pooled formula assumes too. 3% allows for simulation granularity.

cost_per_cup_aggregation.rationale: Fixed before any run. Cost per cup at a given u = (sum over simulated stores of machine + labour + lost-order cost) / (sum of cups served). This is the chain-wide cost per cup, and it matches slide 5 (saving per cup x cups). The alternative, the average of each store's own cost per cup, weights low-demand stores more and is not used for the headline.

peak_utilisation_definition.value: forecast peak-hour arrival rate x surge multiplier, divided by the setup's nominal capacity in that hour, at the base forecast (u = 0, demand = base), before random noise
peak_utilisation_definition.rationale: User check (4): does the fixed-speed mechanism ever bind? Reported for none / moderate / large surge, before the full sweep, alongside the simulated share of orders lost in the peak hours.

crossover_definition.value: smallest u at which mixed cost/cup <= all-machine cost/cup and stays <= for every larger u in the sweep, linearly interpolated between grid points
crossover_definition.rationale: If mixed is cheaper at u = 0: 'no crossover, mixed cheaper everywhere'. If never cheaper: 'no crossover, machines cheaper everywhere'. All-human is plotted and reported but is not part of the headline test.

crossover_stability.rationale: Pass if a crossover exists in at least 18 of 20 seeds and the crossover u differs by at most 10 percentage points across them. If it fails, the slide shows a crossover zone or none, not a single point.

sensitivity.value: one-at-a-time: each parameter with a non-null range set to its low then high value, all others at default; report crossover u (or none) and cost/cup at the slide 2 default u
sensitivity.rationale: Shows which assumptions decide the headline; feeds the 'what could shift the balance' panel and Q&A. No pass/fail.
